what: Ways a measuring instrument returns a plausible wrong answer. Each entry was live in this repository on 2026-09-04, each read GREEN on its first run, and each was caught by something other than the gate that contained it.
whyRecorded: A failing gate announces itself. A mis-scoped gate does not — it returns a number that looks like a finding. Twenty of these in one day is not carelessness; it is the shape of the work, and the shape is worth carrying forward even though none of it is enforceable.
notAGate: This is a document, not a check. Nothing here can be decided mechanically: whether a scan is correctly scoped is a judgement, and a gate that claimed to decide it would be the twenty-first entry.

shapes.name: iterated the wrong object
shapes.instance: ran a battery over LEAN_PROOFS (12 quantum statements) believing it held SEALS (32). Everything passed, meaninglessly.
shapes.tell: a verdict that is uniformly positive across a population you expected to be mixed

shapes.name: mutation that respects a symmetry
shapes.instance: swapping which stroke is positive negated every angle; the invariant 'the bearing closes at zero' survived negation. The probe MOVED and the verdict was still wrong.
shapes.tell: none. No control catches this. Report the negative as a lower bound.

shapes.name: mutation that moves nothing
shapes.instance: inverting every stroke preserves the POSITIONS where polarity changes.
shapes.tell: require each mutation to move its own probe, or the run is an error

shapes.name: resource limit read as refutation
shapes.instance: widening a Lean domain hit maximum recursion depth; read naively that marks honest theorems load-bearing.
shapes.tell: 'could not read it' and 'it is false' need different verdicts

shapes.name: loop bound counted as an assertion
shapes.instance: `r < 2` in a for-header scored as a literal comparison; four seals changed verdict when loop conditions were excluded.
shapes.tell: machinery is not a claim

shapes.name: a scanner reading its own prose
shapes.instance: three times. `\btheorem` matched 'as a theorem is the whole point' and produced a theorem named `is`; once it made a 50-theorem corpus report 0 proven.
shapes.tell: anchor at column zero; a comment mentioning a thing is not the thing

shapes.name: regex over-capture across boundaries
shapes.instance: introduced while fixing the above: scanning to the next declaration swept a bound out of an intervening definition.
shapes.tell: stop at the syntactic end, not at the next occurrence

shapes.name: error sentinel counted as evidence
shapes.instance: a crashed measurement pushed a marker into the fallen-laws list; four constants were reported CONSTRAINED because the harness died.
shapes.tell: a set meaning 'evidence' populated by something meaning 'no information'

shapes.name: output discarded on a noisy exit
shapes.instance: twice. Lean printed every axiom stanza and exited non-zero; the answer was thrown away and the corpus reported 0 proven.
shapes.tell: read the output before believing the exit code

shapes.name: identifier substring replaced instead of the value
shapes.instance: `A432_FREQUENCY = 432` contains 432 twice and the first is in the NAME; the mutation renamed the export.
shapes.tell: replace the last occurrence, or anchor on the declaration

shapes.name: first-match regex hitting a declaration
shapes.instance: twice in one edit: count=1 replaced `function commentsOf(text) {` instead of its call site.
shapes.tell: anchor after a known marker, not on the first occurrence

shapes.name: a default hiding a missing import
shapes.instance: `allCriteria ?? []` printed '0 of 0 criteria met' when the function lived in another module. It is 6 of 7.
shapes.tell: a fallback that cannot be distinguished from a real zero

shapes.name: ledger projection dropping the evidence
shapes.instance: the verdict was right and the reason absent, so pass-by-absence and pass-by-evidence looked identical.
shapes.tell: record what the verdict rests on, not only the verdict

shapes.name: confounded control
shapes.instance: sampling `git status` during a run reported dirty in 848 of 848 samples — my own uncommitted edits.
shapes.tell: scope the control to the measured thing; assert the baseline empty first

shapes.name: a hardcoded list pinned to memory
shapes.instance: three times: the DEFINED names in a generator, the guarded block names in the ratchet, a DOI list. Each was pinned to what its author remembered.
shapes.tell: read it from the source that knows

shapes.name: a sweep narrower than the defect it names
shapes.instance: four standing sweeps read .ts and .mjs and never .lean, while the Lean prose named scripts nothing verified.
shapes.tell: widen only WITH an extractor for the new language, and plant a defect to prove it

shapes.name: shell: a non-matching glob aborts
shapes.instance: zsh nomatch killed a check, so 'found none' and 'never looked' rendered identically.
shapes.tell: use find, not a glob, when absence is a result

shapes.name: shell: unquoted variables do not word-split
shapes.instance: a loop over 19 names ran once over one blob and printed one result.
shapes.tell: read line by line

shapes.name: a comment that terminates itself
shapes.instance: a JS block comment describing comment syntax contained the sequence that closes it.
shapes.tell: quoting a delimiter inside its own form

shapes.name: theory before measurement
shapes.instance: correct arithmetic for a bottleneck (324 child processes), wrong conclusion. Timed one process first: the two gates I had exonerated were 81% of the chain.
shapes.tell: a count is not a cost

shapes.name: asking a registry the wrong kind of question
shapes.instance: the Crossref Funder Registry indexes organisation NAMES; querying it with research topics returns zero, which reads as 'no funder works here'.
shapes.tell: an empty result from a registry that cannot answer the question

shapes.name: enumerate-and-invoke over an unread surface
shapes.instance: a probe called all 327 quantum exports with (1), including publishToZenodo. It threw before any network call and nothing was published — luck, not care.
shapes.tell: never call what you have not read; use an allowlist of pure constructors

principles: Pinned is not forced. A check holding the expected answer as a literal falls for a convention as readily as for a law.
The arbiter must exclude the subject. A predicate inside the thing it tests falsifies by construction and reports green, vacuously.
Err in the unflattering direction and say so. Where an instrument is blunt, choose the bound that runs against you.
An absent instrument voids; it does not verdict.
The rule is stated at the level of the item and broken at the level of the summary. Nobody is looking up.
A number that has become small is not evidence. Three of us abandoned finders today rather than tune them.
Verify the instrument against a case whose answer you already know, before you trust its report.
